description: Ex-Iran Air Boeing 707-321B, c/n 18958. Long-term exhibit in the outdoor airliner line. Present and in an ordered display layout on Esri World Imagery of 29 October 2025.

Boeing 727-81, c/n 19557, carried on Iranian government charge. Widely reported as a former Imperial-era VIP aircraft; that provenance is repeated in secondary sources and is not independently confirmed here.
Boeing 727-30, c/n 18363, ex-Iranian government fleet. One of two 727s in the museum line.
Boeing 737-270C, c/n 20892, ex-Iraqi Airways airframe later on the Iranian register. Preserved in the airliner row.
Boeing 737-270C, c/n 20893. Second of the ex-Iraqi Airways 737-200Cs held here.
Boeing 737-286, c/n 20498, ex-Iran Air. Preserved airframe in the museum line.
Boeing 737-286C, c/n 20500, ex-Iran Air combi.
Boeing 737-286C, c/n 20740, ex-Iran Air combi.
Boeing 747-2J9F, c/n 21514, ex-Iran Air Cargo. The largest exhibit; its bulk is clearly identifiable in the display line on October 2025 imagery.
Lockheed L-1011-100 TriStar, c/n 193B-1231, last registered in Sierra Leone to Air Universal. Stranded in Iran and retained as an exhibit.
Lockheed L-1011-1 TriStar, c/n 193C-1244, ex-Air Universal of Sierra Leone. Second TriStar preserved here.
Fokker F28-4000 Fellowship, c/n 11135, ex-Iran Aseman Airlines.
Fokker F27-600, c/n 10554, in Islamic Republic of Iran Navy markings. The SN- prefix is the Iranian naval aviation serial style.

Fairchild Hiller FH-227B in Iranian Air Force markings. The contributor database carries this airframe as serial 6-9704 with c/n 566, but both values duplicate the DHC-2 Beaver entries in the same collection, so the identity is treated as corrupt and left blank. A second FH-227 in Iran Aseman colours is also reported on site.
Douglas C-47A, c/n 12680, on the Iranian civil register. Note the same c/n is recorded against the museum's A-26B, so one of the two c/n entries in the source is in error.

Douglas A-26B Invader carrying US civil registration N956R. A secondary museum-listing site gives the underlying USAAF serial as 44-34759; that figure is uncorroborated here and is recorded only as a lead.
North American F-86F Sabre, c/n 176-110, in Imperial Iranian Air Force markings. The only jet fighter confirmed in this collection.
North American T-6G Texan, c/n 182-502, wearing the unusual multi-part Iranian serial 66-1-29.
Kaman HH-43F Huskie, c/n 212. The recorded serial string HH43-9411/7 is the form carried in the contributor database and appears to combine a type prefix with the Iranian serial.

DHC-2 Beaver, c/n 566, recorded as Iranian Air Force 6-9701. Serial left blank because c/n 566 is duplicated against the FH-227 entry in the same source; a secondary list gives an ex-USAF identity of 53-7784, unconfirmed.
DHC-4 Caribou, c/n 52, Iranian Air Force serial 553. The source notes it may now carry the civil marks EP-RAJ.
de Havilland Chipmunk T.10, c/n C1/0140, on the Iranian civil register.
Aero Commander 500S Shrike Commander, c/n 500S-3141, in Iranian Air Force markings.
Aero Commander 500S Shrike Commander, c/n 500S-3143, Iranian Air Force.
Aero Commander 500 on the Iranian civil register. No construction number recorded in the source.
Aero Commander 500B, c/n 500B-1418-149, Iranian civil register.
Aero Commander 680FLP, c/n 680FLP-1509-21.
Rockwell Commander 681, c/n 681-6012, recorded against an Iranian government agency.
Rockwell Commander 681B, c/n 681B-6065. A second 681B associated with the national oil company is also listed on site by a secondary source.
Cessna 310Q, c/n 310Q-0011, Iranian civil register.
Cessna 414, c/n 414-0074, recorded as EP-KID. Serial retained in aliases only pending confirmation the marks are still carried.
Piper PA-22-150 Tri-Pacer, c/n 22-6156.
Piper PA-23-250E Aztec, c/n 27-7305151.
Piper PA-31-350 Navajo Chieftain, c/n 31-7552057.
